description: Python project scaffold for NVIDIA Triton Inference Server — src/ package, pyproject.toml with pyright/ruff config, and Makefile targets for install / typecheck / up / client / health.

buildHints.whenToUse: This layer supplies the Python project wrapper for the Triton family — pyproject.toml metadata, a type-checker baseline, and a Makefile so developers can run common tasks without looking up flags.
firstSteps: make install          # pip install -r requirements.txt (tritonclient + numpy)
make typecheck        # pyright src/ — should be clean out of the box
make up               # docker compose up -d  (pulls ~15 GB on first run)
make health           # curl /v2/health/ready — wait for HTTP 200
make client           # python -m src.client — infer against the identity echo model
gotchas: pyproject.toml sets typeCheckingMode=basic; tighten to strict only after adding py.typed and full annotations throughout src/.
The Makefile uses hard tabs — editors that silently convert to spaces will break make. Most editors detect Makefile type and preserve tabs.
`make install-dev` requires pyproject.toml to be present (supplied by this layer); running it before layer application will fail.
pyright is a dev-only dep; the runtime Triton container has no Python typechecker dependency — requirements.txt stays lean.
model_repository version directories MUST be integers (`1`, `2`, ...). Triton silently skips non-integer dirs like `v1` or `latest`.
config.pbtxt `platform` and `backend` are mutually exclusive per model — use `backend: "onnxruntime"` for ONNX, `platform: "tensorrt_plan"` for TRT plans.
TRT engines (`.plan`) are built for a specific GPU + CUDA + TRT version. An engine built on A100 will not run on H100. Rebuild per deploy target.
architectureNotes: src/__init__.py makes src/ a proper package so `python -m src.client` resolves without a separate __main__.py.
pyproject.toml is the single source of truth for Python version, project name, and dev-tool config — requirements.txt is kept as a flat pip-installable subset for Docker and CI.
The Makefile `health` target hits /v2/health/ready (KServe v2 spec) — not /api/infer, which belongs to the Triton v1 protocol.
